text: Compare and contrast the defences of volenti non fit injuria (consent) and contributory negligence.
Explain and critically analyse each element of the Rule in Rylands v Fletcher. [25]
Explain and evaluate the rules governing recovery for nervous shock in negligence. [25]
Section B
William has recently purchased a building for use as a restaurant. The building needs a lot of
repairs before it can be used. In order to cut costs, William asks his friend, Harry, to carry out
some electrical work. William is aware that Harry is not a qualified electrician and so will do the job
at a lower cost. As Harry is finishing the work, he trips on an uneven floor surface and sustains a
serious back injury.
Harry had made a number of basic errors when he carried out the electrical work and after the
restaurant opens for business an electrical fire breaks out. A customer, Kate, and the chef, Philip,
are injured.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities under occupier’s liability. [25]
Andrew goes to the XYZ cinema to watch a movie with a group of friends. Andrew stretches his
legs under the seat in front and falls asleep. At the end of the movie, Andrew is still asleep and
the man in front of him stands up and folds his seat downwards onto Andrew’s outstretched legs,
causing a deep cut and bruising.
Andrew complains to the cinema manager, who apologises but points out that in 20 years there
has not been a similar incident with the seats.
Andrew goes to the local hospital, where a doctor on duty treats his injuries and administers a
drug to prevent infection. The doctor does not warn Andrew of a potential allergic reaction to the
drug which occurs in a small number of cases. Andrew suffers an allergic reaction and is unable to
work for six months.
Advise Andrew as to his rights and any potential remedies in this situation. [25]
Dimitri plays football for his college team. His team reaches the final of a national competition.
During the first few minutes of the game Dimitri makes a hard but fair tackle on Ed, an opposing
player. Ed suffers an injury in the tackle and cannot continue playing. As he leaves the pitch Ed
threatens to break Dimitri’s legs. Ed has to be held back by his teammates as he goes to kick
Dimitri.
At half-time, as the teams leave the pitch, one of Ed’s teammates, Frank, pushes Dimitri over from
behind and kicks him while he is on the ground. Frank runs into the dressing room. A number of
Dimitri’s teammates stand outside the dressing room and prevent Frank from leaving until the
police arrive.
Advise the parties as to their potential liability in this scenario. [25]
